drafts.title: Find compatible fast chargers on trips and see charging state at a glance
drafts.description: When planning or driving long trips, the vehicle displays which fast chargers along the route are compatible and lets the driver determine the charging state from outside the vehicle in a quick glance.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In 95% of real-route planning tests the navigation shows at least one compatible fast charger at planned stops and provides compatibility and estimated charge time within 10 seconds of a planning query; in a usability test 95% of participants correctly identify the charge-port indicator state (charging, charging complete, fault) from 3 meters in both daylight and night conditions.
assumptions: Access to up-to-date third-party charger metadata (connector types, power levels, payment/membership requirements) via cloud services
Navigation/route planner can query charger network data in real time
Charge port indicator is visible from ~3 meters and uses distinct visual states that users can learn in a short test
uncertainties: Coverage and accuracy of third-party charger metadata varies by region and operator
Some legacy chargers may not report live status, reducing visible compatibility even when hardware is compatible

drafts.title: Comfortable ride over broken pavement and low wind-noise at highway speeds
drafts.description: On broken or uneven roads the vehicle should feel composed (not harsh) and on highways above 70 mph wind noise should not be perceived as distracting by occupants.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Over a standardized broken-pavement route, at least 80% of test drivers rate ride comfort ≥ 4/5; on a standardized highway run at speeds ≥ 70 mph fewer than 20% of participants rate wind noise as 'distracting' in blinded passenger trials.
assumptions: Production-level suspension tuning, tyres and aero sealing similar to test vehicles used in trials
Tests use representative vehicle load (2 adults + luggage) and appropriate wheel/tyre specification
uncertainties: Perception of 'harsh' or 'distracting' is subjective and may vary by occupant expectations and road surface severity
Aero noise depends on external factors (wind direction, roadside objects) that add variability to tests

drafts.title: Lane-keeping assist steers smoothly in curves without abrupt corrections
drafts.description: When lane-keeping or highway assist is active, steering interventions should feel smooth and predictable; drivers must not be surprised by abrupt steering corrections in curved road segments.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In standardized highway curve scenarios with lane-keeping active, drivers rate 95% of system steering interventions as 'smooth' or 'natural' and driver-reported occurrences of 'abrupt steering' are ≤ 5% of assisted-curve events in user trials.
assumptions: Tests include representative highway curves, traffic scenarios and lane markings typical for target markets
Driver trials are conducted with drivers who have brief familiarization with the system
uncertainties: System behavior may vary with lane-marking quality and environmental conditions, affecting user perception
Different drivers have different thresholds for what they call 'abrupt' steering

drafts.title: Increase real-world single-charge range compared to predecessor (realistic target)
drafts.description: Raise the vehicle’s real-world single-charge driving range so customers experience substantially longer trips between charges compared to the current model.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On a standardized mixed city/highway real-world test cycle the vehicle achieves ≥ 400 miles single-charge range in the tested standard configuration (representative tyres and load).
assumptions: This target assumes continued incremental improvements in pack energy density and vehicle efficiency consistent with industry progress over the next model cycle
Target applies to the BEV variant with standard wheels/tyres and without optional energy-reducing accessories
uncertainties: Achievability depends on battery chemistry, vehicle mass targets and accessory loads (HVAC usage, towing, etc.)
Customer-requested numbers (600–700 miles) exceed what is realistic for this successor; 400 miles aims to balance customer desire and technical realism
